chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Hammad from Zayd al-Shahham said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man shortens (his prayer) when traveling a distance of twelve miles.'

key_terms.اَلرَّجُلُ: The man (referring to the male traveler, often used generically for the individual)
key_terms.اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ مِيلاً: Twelve miles (the specific threshold for this ruling)
key_terms.يَقْصُرُ: Shortens (referring to shortening the four-rakat prayer to two)

ai.seo_question: What is the distance at which a Muslim traveler must shorten their prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the threshold of twelve miles (approximately 43 km) for the validity of *qasr* (shortening) prayers, a metric widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence. It reflects the practical application of divine concession for travelers, balancing spiritual obligation with physical ease, and serves as a foundational text for defining the geographical limits of travel in Islamic law.
